battle.name: 靈、宜、鹽、百之戰
battle.brief: 中文維基「戰爭列表」所列的靈、宜、鹽、百之戰，發生於773年，是南詔內部勢力在靈、宜、鹽、百四地發生的武裝衝突。秦連弩（Repeating crossbow）在公元前200年已列裝，是真實的早期連發弩機型號，其服役開始時間早於本戰役近千年。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 本役不是唐朝與吐蕃之間的邊境戰爭，而是南詔王國內部的一次武力整合。交戰一方是南詔王庭：時值唐大曆八年（773），南詔王閣羅鳳在位，都城太和城在洱海西岸，王庭以蒙舍為核心，向洱海東岸與金沙江南岸一帶兼併諸部，兵源、賦役與號令都收歸王庭節制。另一方是靈、宜、鹽、百四地的割據勢力：這四處是洱海地區內各有城寨、山場與水鹽資源的部族聚落，平日各據一方、只向王庭納貢不供調兵，戰時互相策應，抵抗編制與稅役的整頓。此外，唐朝的劍南邊軍是這場衝突的外部變數：姚州、安寧一線的唐軍與屯田緊貼南詔北境，四地一旦據險自守，唐軍的牽制便無從施力，反過來令王庭更急於拔除這些釘子。南詔自身的象兵、藤牌長刀與弩手，是王庭用來對付寨牆的主幹；四地守軍則靠木柵、土垣與山林地形自保。四地守方並無統一指揮，各城自領首領、各自徵集寨丁，遇敵時以烽火與遊騎互通消息，故能分進合擊而無須全軍集結；王庭一方調度較整齊，但仍受限於山道運兵之難，一處抽兵，四地便有可乘之機。
countriesEn: This engagement was not a frontier war between the Tang and Tibet but a military consolidation inside the kingdom of Nanzhao. One side was the Nanzhao court: in the eighth year of Dali, 773, Nanzhao was ruled by the king Gelofeng, with the capital Tahe city on the western shore of Erhai, and the court built on the Mengshe clan, annexing the tribes of eastern Erhai and the southern bank of the Jinsha; soldiers, taxes and command were all being drawn into the court's hand. The other side was the separate strength holding Ling, Yi, Yan and Bai: these four places were tribal settlements in the Erhai region, each with its own fort, upland pasture and water and salt resources, keeping to itself in normal times, paying tribute to the court but not answering to its levies, and in war supporting one another against the rounding-up of the organisation and the tax load. The Tang frontier army of Jiannan was the outside variable: the Tang garrison and its farms at Yao prefecture and Anning hugged Nanzhao's northern border, and once the four places held their strongholds independently the Tang could not press them at all, which in turn made the court all the more anxious to pull them out. Nanzhao's war elephants, lacquered rattan shields, long knives and crossbowmen were the court's main instruments against the village walls; the garrisons of the four places relied on wooden palisades, earthen ramparts and the mountain terrain to hold on. The four garrisons had no unified command: each town led by its own chief and raised its own village men, keeping in touch by beacon fires and light horse, so that they could strike in combination without ever assembling a single army. The court on the other hand acted with more order, but was still hamstrung by the difficulty of moving troops along mountain tracks, so that every column it detached offered the four places an opening.
people: 本役可確指姓名者只有南詔王閣羅鳳：他自七世紀中葉起統治南詔，本役正落在他統治的中後段，其時南詔正處於向北兼併的高峰，洱海一帶的城邑多已入其版圖，而劍南邊境也正因南詔的壓力而年年增兵。閣羅鳳在位時最重要的工作是編制與號令的統一：蒙舍為主的王庭要在既有部落之上建立可以直接調兵的編制，靈、宜、鹽、百的割據勢力所拒絕的正是這一條。派去討四地的主將，漢文史料不載其名；四地首領的姓名同樣不可考，只能由殘存的地志、墓銘與後世南詔史的追敘中略知其地。中文史籍對此役多以「南詔平四部」「四城歸附」一類概略語句帶過，具體經過幾乎空白，所以本篇的「人物」一段只能以王與體系的層面立論。唐朝方面，此時劍南節度使更替頻仍，云南邊州的屯田與糧餉由劍南供應，兵力卻被北邊的邊務與藩鎮所牽；南詔之亂之所以不被立即壓下，正因為唐廷自顧不暇。八十五年後閣羅鳳去世，異牟尋嗣位，轉向與唐廷交涉求封，局勢才從兵戎轉入盟約。
peopleEn: The only name that can be attached with certainty to this campaign is that of the Nanzhao king Gelofeng: he had ruled Nanzhao since the middle of the seventh century, and the campaign falls in the later part of his reign, when Nanzhao was at the height of its northward annexation and most of the towns around Erhai had already come under its authority, while the Jiannan frontier of the Tang had been reinforcing year upon year against Nanzhao's pressure. The work that mattered most under Gelofeng was the unification of organisation and command: the court, built on the Mengshe, was trying to establish an establishment from which troops could be summoned directly over the older tribal structure, and exactly that was what the separatists of Ling, Yi, Yan and Bai refused. The commander sent against the four places is not named in the Chinese records, and neither are the leaders of the four places themselves; their ground can only be faintly reconstructed from surviving gazetteers, tomb inscriptions and the retrospective narratives of Nanzhao historians. The Chinese books pass over the campaign in summary formulas such as Nanzhao pacified four tribes or four cities came over, leaving the actual course of the fighting almost blank, so this section can argue only at the level of the king and the system. On the Tang side, the military governors of Jiannan were changing repeatedly, the frontier prefectures of Yunnan drew their garrison and provisions from Jiannan, and the troops there were tied down by trouble on the northern frontier and by the power of the provincial commands; the rebellion was not put down at once precisely because the court had its own troubles. Eighty-five years later, in the year of Gelofeng's death, Yimouxun succeeded him and turned to negotiating with the Tang court for recognition, and only then did the situation move from arms to covenant.
kits: 本卡所列的秦連弩並非本役的制式裝備：它是戰國秦人已成熟的弩機技術，比本役早了將近一千年。但它在本役的位置並不虛構——靈、宜、鹽、百四地都是寨城，四地守軍能撐住攻勢的，靠的就是弩把攻城的人壓在牆外。弩與弓的分別在於以機括把拉力存住，射手扣下懸機即可放矢，體力消耗遠低於張弓，因而能長時間輪流射擊；本卡的連弩更把上弦與擊發連成一組，腳踏機括便可反覆發矢，射速又勝一籌。寨牆上的實際配備，通常是蹶張弩與竹木為機的輕弩分層佈置：近牆一排專射攀附之眾，牆頭高處架大弩以遠射象隊與前列。攻城一方的南詔大軍以象為前驅，象披甲、持長刀，撞擊木柵與土垣；步兵隨後舉藤牌（以牛皮為面、塗漆吸水）遮蔽箭矢，蟻附登城，並在夜間以火把與鼓噪掩護換防。南詔長刀形制與漢劍相近，多供斬擊與破柵；箭矢多削竹木、淬毒後施於弓箭，亦有標槍。守方除弩外，還備木柵、鹿角、拒馬、壕溝、落石與滾木，並以寨內井鹽汲水澆灑塵土、以濕草覆地以防火攻；山道運糧靠驢馬馱馱，牛車只行於洱海平川一段。
kitsEn: The Qin repeating crossbow shown on this card was not a standard piece of equipment in this campaign: it is the matured crossbow mechanism of the Warring States Qin, nearly a thousand years before this war. Yet its place here is not imaginary, for Ling, Yi, Yan and Bai were all stockaded towns, and what let the four garrisons hold out was precisely the crossbow keeping the assaulting parties pinned under the wall. A crossbow differs from a bow in that the mechanism stores the draw, so the shooter releases the catch and fires without the effort a bow demands, and can therefore keep up a steady rotation of shooting; the repeating crossbow on this card links cocking and firing into one motion, the trigger being trodden to shoot again and again, which raises the rate of fire once more. The actual deployment on the wall was in layers, with tread-worked crossbows and light bows of bamboo and wood: a rank close to the parapet shooting at the men clinging to the wall, and heavy crossbows set on the higher sections of the rampart to reach the elephants and the leading files. In the attacking force the Nanzhao army drove its elephants forward, armoured and armed with long knives to batter the palisades and earthen ramparts; the infantry followed behind rattan-and-hide shields lacquered against the arrows, climbed the walls in close order, and covered the relief of the forward lines at night with torches and drums. Nanzhao long knives were close in form to Han swords and were used for cutting and for breaking stockades; arrows were usually of bamboo or wood and poisoned before use, and javelins were thrown as well. On the defensive side the garrisons had, besides the crossbows, wooden palisades, abatis, cheval-de-frise, ditches, loose stone and rolling logs, and they used the well water and salt of the enclosure to damp the dust and laid wet grass against fire attack; supplies went up the mountain tracks on donkeys and mules, ox-carts serving only the one stretch of level ground along Erhai.
tactics: 本役的形態是逐一攻取而非一次會戰：南詔王庭無法以一戰而平四地，只能分兵次第而為，而四地守軍最有效的做法恰恰是拒守不出、待王庭疲。城寨一帶的攻防有固定的次第。守方先把寨牆缺口用木柵與藤牌封住，弩手分班輪替，晝夜不停；白日專射城下逼近的象與前列，夜里改射攀附牆頭的散兵，並以長鉤推倒上牆的梯架。待王庭大軍逼近，守方以遊騎焚燒田禾、截斷糧道，甚至退入山林、遷走居民，寧可棄寨也不肯在平地上與象兵正面相撞。攻城一方的部署則是先斷後路再打正面：分兵奪取渡口與山徑，斷掉城寨與外界的聯繫，迫其困守；主力集結後，先以弓箭與標槍覆蓋城牆四周，逼守軍躲進掩體，然後以大象撞柵、步兵舉盾蟻附，最後集中兵力攻一處缺口。破城之後並不窮追，而是分兵搜捕散卒、接收人口與物資，把新得之地編入王庭的部落序列。四地之間曾有互相策應：一方受攻，鄰地以遊騎襲擊攻城隊伍的側後，迫王庭分兵回救，因此整場戰事拖成數度進退的反覆拉鋸。攻城與守城的界線，在南詔並不只在城牆：山道、渡口與鹽井通道同樣是戰線。王庭分兵扼住要道，四地則以熟悉山徑的寨丁在狹窄處設伏，箭矢自兩側落下，令象兵無從施展；破解之道仍是先破其城，四地失去據點，聯防才會瓦解。
tacticsEn: The shape of this campaign was the taking of one place after another rather than a single set-piece battle. The Nanzhao court could not flatten the four places in one stroke and had to take them in succession, while the best answer open to the four garrisons was to refuse battle, hold fast and wait for the court to tire. The fighting around the stockades followed a fixed routine. The defenders first closed the gaps in the rampart with palisades and shields, posted the crossbowmen in shifts to shoot day and night, aimed the day-time fire at the elephants and leading files below the wall, and switched to the scattered men clinging to the parapet by night, hooking the ladders back down with long poles. As the Nanzhao host closed in, the defenders put light horse across the countryside to burn the crops and cut the roads, and would even retire into the hills and move the inhabitants away rather than meet the elephants on open ground. The besiegers worked to sever the rear before the front: columns were detached to seize the fords and the mountain paths in order to cut the towns off from the outside world and force them to endure, and the main body, once assembled, first covered the walls with arrows and javelins to drive the defenders under cover, then brought the elephants in against the palisades and the shielded infantry up to the walls, and finally concentrated on a single gap in the wall. Once a town was taken the pursuers did not press on: they split off to hunt stragglers and to take in the people and goods, folding the new ground into the court's tribal establishment. The four places also supported one another: when one was attacked, its neighbours sent light horse against the besiegers' rear and forced the court to divide its force, and for that reason the whole campaign dragged on as a see-saw of advances and withdrawals. The line between attack and defence in Nanzhao did not run only along the walls: the mountain tracks, the fords and the salt-well roads were front lines in their own right. The court detached men to hold the key passes, while the four places used village men who knew the paths to lay ambushes in the narrows, arrows coming down from both sides so that the elephants had no room to work; the answer remained to break the towns first, for once the strongholds fell the chain of mutual support fell apart.
data: 本役可用的數字極少，以下幾項比較可靠，且都只寫可以核對的量度。其一，南詔都城太和城在洱海西岸，即今雲南大理一帶；靈、宜、鹽、百四地分布在洱海東岸至金沙江南岸的交通線上，彼此相距數十里至數百里，具址諸說並存，一般以洱海東岸與鹽井地帶為中心。其二，唐劍南治所在成都，自劍南至南詔都城約一千五百公里，糧秣運補全靠金牛道與南方山道，這條路後來正是南詔反攻劍南的通道。其三，鹽是此役的關鍵物資：四地之中有控鹽井者，雲南鹽井自漢代即是蜀地的重要鹽利所在，王庭若要統一編制與稅入，鹽井是不可放棄的一環。其四，弩的射程按當時通行的度量約在百步上下，寨牆上的弩手因此能覆蓋牆根一帶的攀附者；象披甲撞柵的力道雖大，轉向遲緩，恰恰畏懼密集的箭矢。其五，戰事集中於大曆八年（773）一年之內，四地前後陷落，史籍卻不載其月日先後。至於雙方兵員，漢文史料只有數千、數萬一類的概括，且多指整個南詔的常備與徵發之數，而非此役的實投兵數；各城寨的守軍人數、攻城時的象數與戰損，諸說並存且互相矛盾，本篇不採信任何一組確數。此外，雲南雨季多雨、山路泥濘，運兵與運糧都受影響，戰事的推進自然偏向乾季；不過此役的具體起訖月日仍無可靠記載，不宜斷定其節奏。
dataEn: Very few figures survive for this campaign, and the following are the more reliable ones, and all of them are quantities that can be checked. First, the Nanzhao capital of Tahe city stood on the western shore of Erhai, in what is now the Dali area of Yunnan; Ling, Yi, Yan and Bai lay along the lines of communication between eastern Erhai and the southern bank of the Jinsha, from several tens of li to several hundred li apart, their exact sites being a matter of conflicting accounts and generally taken to centre on eastern Erhai and the salt-well country. Second, the Tang seat of Jiannan was at Chengdu, some 1,500 kilometres from the Nanzhao capital, and all grain and provisions went up the Jinniu road and the southern mountain tracks, the same road that Nanzhao would later use to strike back into Jiannan. Third, salt was the material at stake in this campaign: some of the four places controlled salt wells, and the Yunnan wells had been an important source of salt revenue for the Sichuan region since the Han; if the court was to unify the organisation and the tax intake, it could not leave the wells alone. Fourth, the effective range of the crossbow by the measures then in use was about a hundred paces, so the crossbowmen on the rampart could cover the foot of the wall where the climbers worked; an armoured elephant battering a palisade had great force but turned slowly, and that was exactly what massed arrows could punish. Fifth, the fighting was concentrated within the single year 773, with the four places falling in succession, though the books do not give the order of the months. As for the numbers of troops, the Chinese records give only round figures of thousands or tens of thousands, and those mostly for the whole Nanzhao standing and levy rather than for the forces actually engaged; the garrison strengths of the various towns, the number of elephants brought up and the losses suffered are variously given and mutually contradictory, and no single set is accepted here. Rainy season complicated matters further: the Yunnan rains turned the tracks to mud, and moving men and grain along them suffered accordingly, so that the campaign would naturally have pressed on in the dry season; the exact months, however, are not reliably recorded, and the tempo should not be reconstructed.
cause: 南詔之起，本質上是一個以蒙舍為核心的部族聯盟逐步兼併洱海諸部的過程；到閣羅鳳的年代，王庭的疆域擴張已近尾聲，接下來最緊要的不是占地，而是把散在各地的部落、兵源與稅入收編成一套可以直接下令的編制。靈、宜、鹽、百四地之所以拒絕納編，各有各的理由：佔有山場與水脈者怕失去自立之資，控鹽井者怕稅入被王庭抽走，據交通要道者怕失去居間之利。四地之間既已形成互相呼應的關係，王庭要逐個突破就必然付出很高的代價。外部壓力則令這場衝突提前爆發：唐朝劍南邊軍屯於姚州、安寧一線，既是南詔北進的阻力，也是四地可以借力的外援；只要南詔與唐軍的邊界僵持，四地就有餘地拒絕徵調。而唐廷當時自顧不暇——藩鎮坐大，劍南節度使更替頻仍，北邊又有吐蕃牽制，南詔得以在唐廷無力介入的窗口內動手。宗教與王權的變化亦在同期：南詔諸城與外來僧人往來漸密，佛寺與塔開始在洱海沿岸興起，王庭藉統一編制鞏固對各部的號令。
causeEn: The rise of Nanzhao was in substance the slow annexation of the tribes around Erhai by a clan league built on the Mengshe; by Gelofeng's time the territorial expansion was nearly complete, and the pressing business was no longer taking land but drawing the scattered tribes, soldiers and tax revenues together into an establishment that could actually be ordered. The four places of Ling, Yi, Yan and Bai each had their own reason for refusing: those holding upland pasture and watercourses feared losing the basis of their independence, those holding the salt wells feared the court taking the revenue, those sitting on the roads of communication feared losing the profit of being intermediaries. Because the four were already linked in mutual support, the court had to pay a high price to break them one by one. Pressure from outside brought the conflict to a head early: the Tang frontier army of Jiannan, garrisoned at Yao prefecture and Anning, was both the obstacle to Nanzhao's northward advance and the ally the four places could lean on, and as long as the Tang and Nanzhao border stayed frozen the four had room to refuse the levy. The Tang court, meanwhile, could not spare attention, with the provincial commands grown strong, the military governors of Jiannan changing one after another, and Tibet tying down the north; Nanzhao could therefore move inside a window in which the Tang would not intervene. Change in religion and kingship ran alongside: intercourse between Nanzhao's cities and foreign monks grew, temples and pagodas began to rise along the shores of Erhai, and the court used the unified establishment to tighten its hold on the tribes.
impact: 這場戰爭的結果，是南詔王庭把靈、宜、鹽、百四地收進自己的編制，取得沿洱海東岸與鹽井地帶的交通與財源，內部整合因此邁出關鍵一步。統一起來之後的南詔反而更能集中力量對外：劍南方向的壓力自此長期化，蜀中自姚州、安寧至茂、雅一線的城防與屯田年年加緊，金牛道上的運糧與守備成為唐廷的常年開支，而南詔的兵鋒得以不斷前推。同一時期，南詔的內政與信仰格局也在變化：與外來僧人的往來更密，洱海沿岸的佛寺與塔相繼興起，大理一帶的三塔遺存即是這段時期的見證；唐廷與南詔的關係也因南詔新王的取向而改變，異牟尋嗣位後轉向遣使唐廷求封，最終以盟約替代單方面兵戎，劍南的邊患由急戰轉為撫綏並置。由考古一面看，洱海沿岸的城址、墓葬與鐵器出土，使這段南詔內部整合的過程不再只靠文字記載，而有可以與地面痕跡互相對照的實物。統一亦改變了南詔與唐廷交涉的籌碼：四地既已入版圖，王庭在鹽利與兵源上更有餘裕，不必再顧慮內部牽制，於是可以選擇交涉而不是一味用兵；劍南的將領也第一次體會到，眼前的對手不再是一群各自為政的部族，而是一個可以統一下令的政權。
impactEn: The outcome of this war was that the Nanzhao court drew Ling, Yi, Yan and Bai into its establishment and gained the lines of communication and the revenue of the salt-well country along eastern Erhai, which carried the internal consolidation forward by a decisive step. A Nanzhao made whole could concentrate its strength outwards all the more: the pressure on the Jiannan direction became a long-term condition, the defences and garrison farms of the Sichuan interior from Yao prefecture and Anning through Mao and Ya were reinforced year upon year, and the transport of grain and the guarding of the Jinniu road became a standing charge on the Tang treasury, while Nanzhao's spearhead kept moving forward. At the same time the internal government and religious landscape of Nanzhao was changing: intercourse with foreign monks grew denser, temples and pagodas rose one after another along the shores of Erhai, and the three pagodas at Dali preserve visible witness of that period; relations between the Tang and Nanzhao also shifted with the new Nanzhao king's choice of policy, for Yimouxun on his accession turned to sending envoys to the Tang court seeking recognition, and a covenant eventually replaced one-sided armed conflict, the Jiannan trouble being managed part by firmness and part by conciliation. On the archaeological side, the excavated town sites, burials and ironwork along Erhai mean that this internal consolidation of Nanzhao no longer rests on written record alone, but can be checked against the traces left on the ground. Unity also changed the bargaining position of Nanzhao towards the Tang court: with the four places drawn in, the court had more margin in salt revenue and in soldiers and no longer had to weigh against them an internal drag, and could therefore choose negotiation rather than nothing but force. The generals of Jiannan likewise learned for the first time that the opponent before them was no longer a scatter of tribes each acting for itself, but a power that could give a single order.
result: 就本役的直接結果而言，四地先後平定或歸入王庭編制，靈、宜、鹽、百一線的城寨、山場與鹽井盡歸南詔掌握，洱海東岸的交通線自此連成一體，南詔的內部整合向前推進一大步。代價同樣不小：攻城與守城的消耗、寨邑的破壞、逃散與被俘的丁口，都使王庭在統一之後仍需相當時間恢復元氣，這也是此役之後劍南方向的攻勢一度緩和的原因。然而把時間拉長看，統一起來的南詔並非就此休兵：編制一經理順，兵源與稅入便可集中使用，劍南邊患反而由四地內戰的牽制狀態，轉為可以長期施加的邊疆壓力，直至新王改弦更張、以盟約換取太平。史料對此役的記載十分有限：起訖月日、先後次序、雙方兵數與具體經過，多不可考，中文史籍往往只以概略語句帶過，四地之名的具址亦有諸說並存；因此上述判定只能以框架為準，具體細節仍待更多考古與出土文獻補證。從後世看，靈、宜、鹽、百四地在南詔編制中的位置，多只能靠後來的地志與地名沿革推想；其名雖見於戰爭列表，戰役本身卻幾乎被史家略去，這正是本篇不得不以框架陳述、而不去編造具體戰果與人名的原因。
resultEn: As to the immediate result, the four places were pacified in succession or brought into the court's establishment, the towns, uplands and salt wells of Ling, Yi, Yan and Bai passed to Nanzhao, and the line of communication along eastern Erhai was joined into one, so that the internal consolidation of Nanzhao moved a long way forward. The cost was not small: the wear of siege and defence, the destruction of the settlements, and men lost, scattered or captured left the court needing time to recover its strength even after the victory, which is why the pressure on the Jiannan front eased for a while afterwards. Over a longer span, however, a reunited Nanzhao did not rest. Once the organisation was set in order the soldiers and the revenue could be concentrated, and the trouble on the Jiannan frontier changed from a situation held in check by the internal fighting into a border pressure that could be applied for years to come, until the new king changed course and exchanged the wars for a covenant and peace. The surviving records of this campaign are very thin: the months, the order of the fighting, the numbers engaged and the course of the operations are largely unrecoverable, and the Chinese books pass over it in summary formulas, while the exact sites of the four places are variously given. The judgements above can therefore only be taken as the frame of what is known, with the finer detail still waiting on archaeology and on newly excavated texts. From later times, the place of Ling, Yi, Yan and Bai within the Nanzhao establishment can only be inferred from later gazetteers and the changing fates of place names; the names survive in the lists of wars while the fighting itself was passed over by the historians, which is precisely why this account sets out a frame rather than inventing particular results and names.
